Shaftesbury, Anthony Ashley Cooper (1801–85; ODNB), 7th earl of, politician, philanthropist, and social reformer; chairman of the Lunacy Commission 1845–85.
Stanley, Arthur Penrhyn (1815–81; ODNB), dean of Westminster; m., 1863, Lady Augusta Elizabeth Frederica, b. Bruce (1822–1 March 1876; ODNB), lady-in-waiting, secretary, and friend of Queen Victoria.

Stanley, Henrietta Maria, b. Dillon (1807–95; ODNB), m., 1826, Edward John (1802–1869; ODNB; see 12:59TC to JAC, 27 Feb. 1840), 2d Baron Stanley of Alderley, Whig politician; they lived at Alderley Park, Cheshire, and 40 Dover St., London. Both were friends of the Carlyles. They had nine surviving children including Henrietta Blanche (1829–1921), 5th countess of Airlie; Maude (1833–1915; ODNB), women's welfare activist; see 48:24048:biographical notes; John Constantine (see below); and Edward Lyulph (1839–1925; ODNB), educational theorist.

Stanley, Col. John Constantine (1837–23 April 1878), son of Lord and Lady Stanley of Alderley, he m., 1871, Susan Mary Elizabeth, b. Stewart-Mackenzie (1845–1931), niece of Lady Ashburton; they had two das., Madeline Cecilia Carlyle (2 July 1876–1966), and Osma Mary Dorothy (1877–1965); they lived at 37 Wimpole St.

Stephen, James Fitzjames (1829–94; ODNB; see 41:24JWC to TC, 14 Sept. 1864), judge and writer, knighted Jan. 1877. He m., 1855, Mary Richenda, b. Cunningham (1829–1912); they had eight children: Katharine (1856–1924; ODNB), Herbert (1857–1932), James Kenneth (1859–92), Harry Lushington (1860–1945), Helen (1862–1908), Margaret Emily (b. ca. 1862), Rosamond (1868–1951), and Dorothea (1872–1865). Their London home was at 24 Cornwall
Gdns., Queen's Gate. His brother Leslie Stephen (1832–1904; ODNB), author and critic, m., 1867, Harriet Marian, b. Thackeray (1840–28 Nov. 1875; ODNB).

Sterling, John (1806–44; ODNB), writer; he had been a particular friend of TC's; see CL vols. 8–18 and Carlyle's Life of Sterling (1851). He m., 1830, Susannah, b. Barton (1801–43), their children were: Edward Coningham (1831–3 June 1877), m. Lillian Bertha, b. Stone (b. 1844), they had a da. (b. ca. 1869); Julia Maria (1836–1910); John Barton (1840–1926), capt. in the Coldstream Guards, m., 1863, Caroline Matilda, b. Salusbury-Trelawny (1842–1917); and Hester Isabella (1843–1908). His brother was Sir Anthony Coningham Sterling (1805–71; ODNB; see 9:103TC to JAC, 2 Dec. 1836, and later vols.), soldier; m., 1829, Charlotte, b. Baird (d. 1863), who suffered attacks of insanity and was jealous of JWC (see 18:266–67JWC to HW, [12 Nov. 1844], and 19:9JWC to HW, [9 Jan. 1845]).

Stewart, Margaret, b. Austin (1831–74), da. of Mary and James Austin, m., 1859, Thomas Stewart (1832–69), farmer from Hollybush, living at Ernhirst (Ironhirst), about 5½ mi. (9 km.) SW of Dumfries; see 38:19TC to JAC, 1 Dec. 1861; they had a da., Mary (b. ca. 1861), and four sons, William (b. 1863), James (b. 1864), Hugh (b. 1866, dead by April 1868), and Thomas (b. 1869). After Margaret's death her brother James and sister Mary Anne moved to Ernhirst to look after the farm and the children.

Tennyson, Alfred (1809–92; ODNB), poet; poet laureate 1850–92; m., 1850, Emily Sarah, b. Sellwood (1813–96); friends of the Carlyles since the early 1840s. They had two surviving sons, Hallam (1852–1928, ODNB), and Lionel (1854–86). They lived at Farringford, Isle of Wight, and Aldworth, near Haslemere, Surrey.

Tyndall, John (1820–93; ODNB), physicist, prof. of natural philosophy at the Royal Institution, Albemarle St., London, from 1853; TC's admirer and friend from the mid-1850s; see 31:1–2TC to JF, 2 Jan. 1856. He m., 29 Feb. 1876, Louisa Charlotte, b. Hamilton (1845–1940), eldest da. of Lord Claud Hamilton (1813–84), and his wife, m. 1844, Lady Elizabeth Emma, b. Proby (1821–1900).

Venturi, Emilie (ca. 1819–93; ODNB), da. of William Henry Ashurst (ca. 1791–1855; ODNB; portrait painter); supporter of Italian independence and campaigner for women's rights; unhappily m. to Sydney Hawkes, whom she divorced 1861; see 30:215 and 235JWC's Journal. She m., 1861, Carlo Venturi (ca. 1830–66). A strong supporter of Giuseppe Mazzini, and the Young Italy movement, she published various English editions of his writings and Joseph Mazzini: A Memoir (1875). Friend of the Carlyles for many years.
Victoria (1819–1901; ODNB), queen of Great Britain and Ireland 1837–1901; m., 1840, Albert (1819–61; ODNB), prince consort.

Vigfusson, Gudbrand (1827–89; ODNB), prominent scholar of medieval
Scandinavian history, currently living in Oxford; friend of John A. Carlyle's.

Warren, Sarah (b. ca. 1812 in Norfolk), a widow with adult children (see 41:96JWC to MR, 17 Nov. 1864), cook and housekeeper at Cheyne Row Nov. 1864–Sept. 1875. Mrs. Warren was previously wrongly identified as Eliza Warren (ca. 1816–1905) in vols. 41 and 42.
Watt, Thomas Fowler (1838–62), stepson of John A. Carlyle; went to Australia, 1861, and d. on his return (see 38:115TC to JWC, 2 July 1862).

Watt, Henry (1839–1913), stepson of John A. Carlyle; at sea from 1854 (see 29:121TC to EE, 22 Dec. 1854), then master mariner and shipowner in Liverpool; he m., 1863, Jane Wilson, b. Hunter (1837–1908), da. of John Hunter (1801–69; see 8:161TC to MAC, [1 July] 1835) and Helen, b. Vary (1804–85), old friends of John A. Carlyle's; Helen Hunter now lived at Kingsmuir House, Peebles, Scottish Borders. By 1875 Henry and Jane had seven children, and by 1877 they were living at Victoria Park, Wavertree, Liverpool.

Watt, Arthur Chorley (1840–85), stepson of John A. Carlyle; joined the civil service 1862, and was currently an Assistant Judge in Poona, India; he m., 1869, Henrietta Vary, b. Hunter (b. 1846), younger da. of John and Helen Hunter (see Henry Watt); they had a da. (b. 1870), and two sons (b. 1873) and (b June).
Watt, William (b. 1842), stepson of John A. Carlyle; an officer in the Dragoons, m., 1866, Mary, b. Smith, da. of E. H. Smith of Grouville, Jersey.
Wellmer, Meta (1826–89; see 43:21TC to MEW, 24 Oct. 1865, and 45:207MAI to MEW, 3 Dec. 1868), German writer, teacher, feminist, vegetarian, and spiritualist. Her publications included Deutsche
Erzieherinnen und deren Wirkungskreis [German Educators and their Sphere of Influence] (Leipzig, 1877), and Geistergeschichten aus neuerer Zeit [Recent Ghost Stories] (Nordhausen, 1875).

Welsh, Alexander (Alick) (b. 1816), son of JWC's maternal uncle John; m., ca. 1849, Sophy, b. Martin (b. ca. 1824). Their children were John (Jackie) (ca. 1853–64), Isabella Helen (b. 1856; see 31:201JWC to TC, 29 Aug. 1856), Margaret (b. 1858), and Jean (b. 1860); they lived at Sandown Park, Wavertree, Liverpool.

Welsh, Ann (1799–10 May 1877), Elizabeth (1792–4 May 1877), and Grace (1801–67), JWC's paternal aunts (see 14:67TC to JWC, 11 March 1842, and 16:219JWC to JW, [26 Jun. 1843]), living at Craigen Villa, Morningside, Edinburgh.
Welsh, Grace, b. Welsh (1782–1842), JWC's mother; m., 1800, John Welsh (1776–1819; see 1:202–3JBW to EWE, 5 Oct. 1819), JWC's father, doctor in Haddington.

Welsh, John (1785–1853; see 28:286–87JWC to HW, 12 Oct. 1853), JWC's maternal uncle, brass and copper founder, who had lived at 20 Maryland St., Liverpool; m., 1808, Mary, b. Colliver (d. 1838; see 10:200TC to AC, 15 Oct. 1838); their children were Helen (ca. 1813–53); Walter; Alexander; Jeannie (1818–95), m., 1853, Andrew Chrystal (ca. 1811–83), wine merchant from Glasgow, they had a da., Mary (1857–1937); see 40:226–2740:biographical notes; John (1820–60); Margaret; and Mary.

Welsh, Margaret (Maggie) (1821–29 April 1875), da. of JWC's maternal uncle John; lived in Auchtertool with her brother Walter. She was JWC's nurse, Dec. 1863–May 1864, and helped look after TC after JWC's death, late April–mid- Aug. 1866, and June–Oct. 1867, and continued to visit regularly thereafter.

Welsh, Mary (1823–Sept. 1879), da. of JWC's maternal uncle John; usually lived in Auchtertool with her brother Walter, but had been living in the Perth Asylum since 1869 to try to recover from her opium addiction.

Welsh, Rev. Walter (1815–17 Dec. 1879; see 16:12JWC to JW, [8 Jan. 1843]), son of JWC's maternal uncle John; minister at Auchtertool, Fife, since 1842. His sisters Margaret (Maggie) and Mary usually lived with him.

Wilson, Thomas (b. 1811; see 22:xiii22:introduction, and 26:30426:biographical notes), scholar, old friend of TC's, now teaching in Weimar; see 40:23540:biographical notes, and 47:73–74TC to AC, 6 Oct. 1870. He m., 1861, a German wife, unidentified further.
